claim: Defines the atomic punch event e as a structured 7-tuple of temporal attributes (start/end frames) and categorical attributes (hand, distance, technique, target, effectiveness), the foundational discrete unit of the boxing analysis system.
equation: e = (t_{start}, t_{end}, a_{hand}, a_{dist}, a_{tech}, a_{target}, a_{eff})

claim: Declares the per-boxer learnable embedding E_b as a real matrix of latent feature dimension D by time-order C, capturing the boxer's latent standing within the global competitive network.
Models the boxer's time-evolving latent embedding E_b(t) as a polynomial in time of order C-1 with learned coefficient matrices, capturing how a fighter's standing evolves over time.

Defines the match-level fused feature F_match as the output of an MLP applied to the concatenation of both boxers' indicator profiles and temporal embeddings, modeling the interaction between the two fighters.
Defines the multi-task training loss as a weighted sum of mean-squared error on predicted technical indicators and cross-entropy on match outcome, with weights alpha and beta.

Defines the strategy gradient G_b as the vector of partial derivatives of predicted win probability with respect to each of the 18 technical-tactical indicators, used to rank which adjustments raise winning chances.
Defines long-range distance as a spatial interval greater than one full arm length, a zone where the boxer must use footwork to bridge the gap before delivering a strike.
Defines mid-range distance as the interval between half and full arm length, where effective straight punches or hooks can land from a stationary stance.
Defines close-range (infighting) distance as less than half an arm length, where the boxer relies on short-range mechanics such as uppercuts.
Declares the punch-detection model input X as a tensor of T frames by J joints by 5 pose channels (2D and 3D pose estimates).
Defines the per-frame contextualized feature F as the TCN temporal encoder applied to the reshaped pose input, yielding a T-by-d feature matrix.
Defines the anchor-free detection head output at time t as the punch probability p_t and the start/end time shifts b_t^s and b_t^e relative to the current frame.
Represents each detected punch E_t as a triple of its probability, inferred start time, and inferred end time derived from the head's time-shift outputs.
Declares the input RGB video V as a tensor of T frames by H-by-W spatial resolution by 3 color channels.
Declares the learnable pose-region mask V_PRG, encoding 2D pose and hit-region positions, as a tensor matching the video dimensions.
Defines the skeleton-stream feature F_s from the TCN skeleton encoder and the video-stream feature F_v from the I3D video encoder applied to the pose-masked video, with dimensions d_s and d_v.
equation: F_s = f_s(\text{reshape}(X, [T, J \times 5])) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_s} ; F_v = f_v(V + V_{PRG}) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v}

claim: Declares the mixture-of-experts router weight matrix w as an H-by-4 real matrix assigning each of H experts a weight for each of the 4 punch attributes.
Computes the mixture-of-experts router weights w by applying softmax to the router MLP's output on the concatenated skeleton and video features.
Aggregates the punch-attribute prediction y_i as the router-weighted sum of the H experts' outputs on the concatenated features, for each of the 4 attributes.
Defines the Pearson correlation coefficient r_k between estimated and ground-truth values of the k-th technical indicator across boxers, used to evaluate prediction reliability.

Defines the advantage probability p_b^(k) as the maximum of two probabilities: that the boxer's KDE indicator distribution exceeds the weight-class level distribution, and that a joint 2D KDE sample favors the boxer over historical opponents.
Defines the paired sample (u,v) as drawn from the 2D kernel density estimate over the boxer's and opponents' k-th indicator values, used in the advantage-probability comparison.
